Starting in 2004, I left my relatively comfortable American home and traveled to South America for a little over a year. Mainly I spent my time in Peru, but I also spent a bit of time in Bolivia, Chile, and Argentina. While I was in the Andes mountains of Peru in a city called Juliaca, I had some of the strangest and scariest experiences of my life. Of these, this one stands out as the most disturbing.

It was late at night. Ordinarily, I tried not to be out on the street in the more desolate areas of town much after eight or nine. To be out later than that was to be inviting a mugging, even if you are a big guy (6'4", 240) like me. This night, though, I found myself out visiting a friend I had made who had fallen ill and was bed-ridden. It was almost eleven by the time I realized the hour, and so I bid a hasty farewell and started on the long trek across the city back to the house at which I was staying.

During the daylight hours, it would have been simple for me to find a tri-cycle taxi called a "trici" (tree-see) which would have gotten me home in about twenty minutes. At this time of night, though there was no hope of encountering any sort of taxi to take me home. I was going to have to walk, which would likely make it a forty-five minute trip. Figuring I wanted to get home as quickly as possible, I struck out at a fairly quick pace.

As I walked along the deserted dirt roads, it struck me just how cold it was. Being 14,000 feet above sea level, it would often get chilly at night even during the summer, but here we were in October and it was downright cold, and it seemed to be getting colder. I shivered against the cold and picked up my pace even more.

I got to a cross street that would lead me almost straight back to my house and turned the corner where I suddenly encountered a wall of fog. It was incredibly surreal. One minute on one street there was no fog, but upon turning a corner I was met with a seemingly impenetrable wall. I paused for a moment and considered going around a different way, but not wanting to be out on the street any later than absolutely necessary, I took a deep breath and walked into the shroud of fog.

Inside the fog it was obviously colder. I began shivering almost uncontrollably as I penetrated deeper and deeper. After about five minutes, I had the impression that someone was behind me. I paused and listened, but heard nothing. The soft glow of the weak streetlights overhead barely provided any relief from the fog and I could see nothing unless it was within about five feet of me.

I waited a moment, and proceeded onward. Again, I heard it. Not the steady crunching sound of footsteps, but something else. It sounded as if something were being dragged. It was a light constant crunch against the stone and dirt that made up the road. I walked faster hoping that I could simply outpace whatever it was behind. Still, I could hear it coming on. It got no farther away and it got no closer. Still, I couldn't see anything for the fog.

After a few minutes that felt like an eternity, I broke into a run for the nearest cross street. Still the dragging, crunching sound stayed right behind me. I raced toward the next street and took a hard left, sprinting faster than I ever had before or have since. Still the fog was with me, and still the crunching continued. I raced down the street. I looked behind me and the thick fog continued to stretch down the street, the crunching still back there. As I sprinted past the next street, the fog suddenly ended. The world seemed flood with light as the streetlights above me glowed down onto me. I skidded around a corner and stopped. I was breathing hard, but managed to control my breathing and listen for the crunching sound. I was maybe fifty feet from where I had left the fog, and around a corner on a deathly silent street, but there was no sound except the rasping of breathing in the thin mountain air. I glanced around the corner to see if anything was there and was shocked by what I found. There was absolutely no fog anywhere to be found.

This isn't a recent occurrence but I want to contribute more to the subverse, and this is a perfect real life story to tell. This story involves my best friend and I when we were at College, but the start of it actually goes way back into my High School Years.

My first High School job involved working with a group of other teenagers, and one of them I will call Fat Sarah. To this day I'm not sure why they even thought hiring this enormous girl was a good idea. She was wider than she was tall, and probably weighed a good 250 pounds then. When ever she talked she always talked about food. It was pretty clear she came from a family of whales. The way she talked they had feasts every day. They apparently cooked whole turkeys (fried actually) on a regular basis, and her favorite food apparently was fried turkey leg and cheesy mash potatoes. Sometimes she'd bring her own lunch and it consisted of the worst home-made food possible. I remember the smell used to make me gag. She's straight eat it all cold too.

If she wasn't talking about food, then she was talking about her current celeb crushes. Due to her weight she couldn't actually pull her own weight so it was up to the rest of us to do her job. She constantly complained about being tired, too hot, or hungry. When that job ended I thought I would never see her again.

Then College happened, and she ended up sharing a class. She had since I had last seen her put on at least an additional 100 pounds. It was pure labor for her to even get to class and she barely fit into the seats. She was also often followed by her best friend, I'm going call her Mini Moo. Mini Moo was probably a good 200 pounds but smaller than Fat Sarah. A moon to a planet really to compare.

One day she brought up the topic of Twilight (the book series) and ask us what our honest opinion was about it. I told them I have no interest in reading it, as it's not my kind of thing. My friend gave an honest and civil critique against the book and why. This apparently really really set off Fat Sarah. She got angry and started yelling, and then the professor told her to stop or she'd have to leave.

After the end of the class we rushed to get out well ahead so we wouldn't have to deal with them. Unfortunately we got stuck behind people, and by the time we made it to the stairs they had too. They actually got behind us, and the larger whale tried to push my best friend down the stairs by "bumping her aggressively". She failed of course because my friend caught her balance, I had wanted to go to the security guard about it but my best friend didn't want to deal with it. Plus we had another class to catch. If she ever did anything like that again, she agreed we would be talking to the campus about it.

For a few weeks afterwards they both stalked us during our break/lunch. We had a few favorite spots to go to that they couldn't, but sometimes we'd eat closer just to have a laugh at their really silly behavior. They'd show up like 15 minutes after we sit down all out of breath, sit, and just stare at us with mad looks. It wasn't every day but often enough to notice. One day the fat bitch stopped showing up, and then it was just the Mini moo that stalked us but she behaved differently. One day it was just me because friend didn't make it to class that day, and Mini Moo was there too. She kept getting up and sort of walking towards me and then going back and sitting down.. She looked like she wanted to say something to me but wouldn't. So I figured, what the hell I should talk to her. I did. Turns out she and Fat Sarah had a big argument/falling out. Mini Moo didn't say much about why, other than Sarah being mad at her for mentioning they should both focus on losing some weight. Mini Moo did mention that Sarah probably won't be around anymore as she is no longer able to actually make it to class. The whole reason Mini Moo kept following us after Fat Sarah was gone, is to apologize apparently.

The story doesn't end here. Years later I was at work and these two horrendously fat things stomped slowly in, and I just barely recognized Fat Sarah. She had somehow managed to put on even more pounds. Her body was so grossly disfigured I wasn't entirely sure it was her until she started talking. She didn't recognize me but wanted to buy some animals. She yelled at the other obese thing (I think it was either a boyfriend, or a brother), to go get her wallet because "she ain't paying for the animals with her pretty looks". It was so hard to not burst out laughing and go "What pretty looks? Are you trying to impress a male rhino or something?".

Since then I have not seen her. I have seen the guy who came with her that day, and when I asked about her he told me she doesn't leave home anymore because it's too hard so he does all the shopping now. I'm pretty certain now she's horrendously bed-bound. Honestly it still horrifies me to think back. This girl obviously got a lot of the early problems from having a ham family....but at some point she could have looked in the mirror and went "Nope! I need to change". She didn't. It makes make sad because with FA and HAES in full swing now there are going to be a lot of kids who go this same route. That's one of my many stories I have to share.
Assaulted over Twilight: Tale of how a moon became a planet

Pretty much. It was so much like a series of pictures every time I saw her. Snap one photo, she's already beginning to feel the aches and pains of being obese. Snap next picture, she's now finding out a lot of things were not made to fit a person that is 10 times bigger than a normal person. Snap next picture, she's getting ready to have full blown knee/heart/lung collapse and can barely waddle. Her IQ had dropped so badly she doesn't even recognize people she used to hate/stalk.

The final two pictures are no doubt her bed bound, and then either cremated, or in an extra wide coffin.
Question: What happened to mini-moo? Did she make it?

I honestly don't know for sure. She talked to me one more time once, and asked me what are things she can do to lose weight. After that she stuck to her own corner in class. She did seem to take some talking points to heart. She stopped coming into class with giant sugar drinks. She usually had water, or tea from a local tea place near-by. I never saw her eat...but that was an improvement. Before, when Fat Sarah was around they would always camp right near the door before class, and always have some large bags of super greasy bad food. After class it was my routine to cut through a certain area on campus on way to next class, (after taking a light lunch of course, or at least a break) and the two used to always be around a certain spot inside with more bad food. That I stopped seeing too.

Initially she seemed to be losing weight during the rest of semester. After that I never saw her again. I always hoped that without Fat-Sarah around she would have had the drive to actually become human sized. That's a big reason why so many people in fat circles never lose weight. They are always around enablers who pull everyone else down who might even consider exiting Club Fat.
I feel like maybe Mini Moo could have turned it around and made better choices and lost the extra weight. I like to think I'm optimistic.

I would like to hope the same. Nine times out of then it's been pointless to be optimistic about people and fixable flaws in my experience. A lot of people don't want to recognize huge problems they need to work on to better themselves, or if they do it's a short lived thing. One can always hope though.
